rationale: The chapter's method (uniform OT symbolic definitions established by multiple independent witnesses) applied to the supplied texts yields a coherent identification of 'the truth' as God's law/word as the standard itself. Psalm 119:142 supplies the direct equation ('thy law is the truth'), corroborated by John 17:17 ('thy word is truth') and integrated with the three titles of John 14:6 via Solomon's triad in Proverbs 6:23. This accounts for the definite article, the entry's printed references, and the cross-symbol mechanics better than the common personification-first reading, which treats the law-identification as secondary or metaphorical rather than definitional. Secondary elaborations (Torah-embodied person, highway/door/veil, freshly-slain way) are consistent extensions but not required for the core referent and remain open to dispute.
book_core_identification: The truth is God's law (the word) as the standard/measure itself.
book_secondary_elaborations: Jesus is the truth as the living, embodied Torah/standard walking in the flesh.
The three titles (way/truth/life) form one Torah reality seen from three angles (standard, conduct, existence).
The truth (law/word) is inscribed on the doorposts of the door that is Christ, together with the blood of the lamb.
The flaming sword keeping the way of the tree of life is the word of God.
Hebrews 10:20's prosphatos way is freshly slain and living, identifying the road with Christ's flesh.
strongest_counter_interpretation: In the dominant Johannine and mainstream Christian reading, 'the truth' is primarily God's self-revelation and divine reality personified in Jesus Christ himself (John 14:6 as the controlling claim), such that knowing the truth means knowing him; God's word/law is true and sanctifying (John 17:17; Ps 119) but is not definitionally identical to 'the truth' as a fixed symbolic referent independent of Christ.
counter_core_identification: The truth is God's self-revelation and divine reality supremely embodied in the person of Jesus Christ.
material_core_denial: The counter denies that 'the truth' is definitionally God's law as the standard itself; it treats the law/word as true/faithful revelation that points to or is fulfilled in Christ rather than as the primary referent of the definite noun.
counter_case: John 14:6 places the definite claim 'I am ... the truth' in Jesus' mouth, making the person the controlling referent.
John 1:14, 17 and 8:31-32 link grace/truth and liberating knowledge of the truth directly to the incarnate Word and his teaching.
Ephesians 4:21 ('the truth is in Jesus') and the Spirit-of-truth passages (John 14-16) reinforce a Christocentric/pneumatological center rather than a Torah-equation.
Common reading integrates Ps 119:142 and John 17:17 as affirming that God's word is true, not that 'the truth' is definitionally the law as a free-standing symbol.
book_explanatory_advantages: Supplies an explicit equative text (Ps 119:142: 'thy law is the truth') that the book treats as definitional rather than merely descriptive.
Accounts for the definite article and the uniform symbolic method already demonstrated on the parables (multiple independent OT witnesses).
Integrates John 17:17, Proverbs 6:23, and the entry's own printed references (Ps 119:142; 2 John 4) into one consistent standard/measure without requiring later personification as primary.
Explains why 'the truth' can function as the measure that sanctifies and against which everything else is weighed, independent of any single NT claim.
counter_explanatory_advantages: Gives direct weight to the first-person claim of John 14:6 as the most prominent and most-quoted occurrence.
Aligns with the broader Johannine cluster (Word made flesh full of grace and truth; Spirit of truth; knowing the truth sets free) that centers the person.
Avoids reducing the personal claim to an embodiment of a prior abstract standard.
decisive_sources: Psalms 119:142 — Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.
John 17:17 — Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.
Proverbs 6:23 — For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life.
John 14:6 — I am the way, the truth, and the life (read via the OT-defined symbols).
unresolved_objections: Whether the personal embodiment claim of John 14:6 must be treated as primary rather than as the living expression of the already-defined standard.
How fully the secondary personification, door/highway, and prosphatos elaborations are required by the texts versus optional extensions of the core.
Whether 2 John 4's 'walking in truth' more naturally supports the gospel/doctrine or moral-conduct reading than the law-as-standard reading.
